subject: Re: Deployment options — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finsecure.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment options — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand FinSecure's production constraints. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation for customer PII and model-inference logs (no cross-customer co-mingling).
- Preferred option if possible: Private VPC or on-prem (customer-managed network, KMS).
- Acceptable alternative: Dedicated capacity if we can guarantee isolated GPU pools, customer-managed encryption keys, and strict audit logging.
- Must-have security artifacts: SOC 2 evidence, network diagrams, and data-retention controls for audit.

Clarifying questions for your security team (so we scope the POC right):
1) Is customer-managed KMS required, or is Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) optional?
2) Any regulatory constraints that require zero egress of raw inference logs (i.e., must stay inside customer VPC)?
3) Expected retention window for inference logs and whether aggregated metrics are permitted off-VPC.

Attachments in this thread:
- SOC2_summary.pdf (summary of Redwood's SOC 2 scope)
- private-deployment-architecture.pdf (high-level VPC/on-prem topology)
- redwood-technical-faq.pdf (answers to common Dedicated vs Private questions)

Proposed next steps:
- Security deep-dive (30–45m) with your infosec and our infra/security lead (Mateo). Suggested times: Wed or Thu morning PST.
- We can scope a narrow POC for Private VPC (customer-managed control plane) or an equivalent Dedicated canary if timeline prohibits full Private.
- I’ll loop Mateo to provide kernel/ops constraints and a short tech checklist we’ll need for a sizing doc.

If this looks right, I’ll book the security sync and include a short pre-read.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0137

On the call today: Alex, Priya, Marissa (R.I.), Mateo (infra lead — joined for last 10 min)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Deployment options — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. This captures things well. Quick answers while I loop in our security lead: 

1) BYOK is strongly preferred; I think we can make exceptions but our standard is customer-managed keys for production.
2) Zero egress is a preference for some business units — they require that raw inference logs never leave the customer network. Aggregated telemetry (token counts, latency p95) is acceptable off-VPC.
3) Retention: default 90 days for raw logs, 1 year for aggregated metrics; some teams need 30-day retention for raw logs.

Can we confirm whether the Dedicated capacity option can support BYOK and network isolation at the subnet level? If Dedicated still routes logs through Redwood-managed control plane (even if in a dedicated pool), that may not work for the stricter BU.

Happy to meet Wed 10am PT if that works for Mateo and your infra/security folks.

Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Security, FinSecure Inc.
alex.morgan@finsecure.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finsecure.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment options — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Alex —

Perfect, thanks for the quick answers. Short notes ahead of the security deep-dive: 

- BYOK: we support customer-managed keys for both Private and Dedicated, but the implementation differs: Private VPC can use a customer VT (e.g., AWS KMS in their account) for both model storage and logs; Dedicated can integrate with BYOK for storage and S3 buckets but the control plane for routing/monitoring remains Redwood-managed unless you opt for our Private control plane add-on. We’ll outline specifics on Wed.

- Zero egress: Private VPC (VPC peering or PrivateLink) can be configured such that raw inference traffic and raw logs never leave the customer's VPC. For Dedicated, we typically stream telemetry to Redwood telemetry endpoints; we can offer a no-egress contract for the POC but it needs legal/SLA review.

- Retention: we can scope variable retention per environment. For the POC, we’ll propose 30/90/365 day presets and show how to configure retention policies for raw logs vs aggregated metrics.

I’ve attached the SOC 2 summary and a high-level private deployment architecture doc for your security team to scan.

Next steps: I’ll schedule Wed 10am PT for the security sync with Mateo + our security PM. Please confirm attendees and I’ll send an invite with a short pre-read (the attached docs).

Also noted: Alex — you asked whether Dedicated can meet the strictest BU requirement. We’ll bring a short matrix that maps requirements -> minimal viable deployment (Private VPC recommended for zero-egress; Dedicated with Private control plane might be an acceptable middle ground).

Thanks —

Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Deployment options — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Mateo —

Forwarding the thread from FinSecure. They have strict zero-egress requirements for some BUs and BYOK is preferred. They asked whether Dedicated can provide BYOK + subnet-level isolation; my read is: Dedicated + Private control plane (customer-controlled control plane deployed into their account) can meet most of this but will require an ops/price conversation and likely add-on for control plane deployment. Private VPC is our cleanest yes for zero-egress.

Can you: 
- Prepare a short matrix mapping the specific requirements (BYOK, zero egress, raw log retention, audit logs) to implementation options (Private VPC, Dedicated + Private control plane, Dedicated alone) — 1-pager.
- Call out tech risks/unknowns for the POC (e.g., model weight storage, KV cache persistence, latency impact of customer-side KMS calls).
- Estimate a rough POC timeline and any infra lead time we should flag to the customer.

I’ll send the Wed invite once I hear back (aiming 10am PT).

Thanks —

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
